48eae6652508275bf04c0e275388f1d97aea2bd9.summary: A 2014 blog post by LogRhythm describes how PowerShell and OSX one-liners can show a fake login prompt to capture plain-text passwords, presented as a proof of concept. It names tools such as PowerShell, PowerSploit, meterpreter and SSH, and closes with defensive advice: restrict SSH and PowerShell Remoting, monitor logs, use filtering proxies with SSL inspection, and segment networks. No threat actors, CVEs or figures are named.

hedges: Presented as a simple proof of concept demonstrating one of many ways to steal plain-text credentials.
The technique can be hit-or-miss depending on the target process and environmental restrictions.
The author describes their PowerShell script as very poorly coded and asks for recommendations.
The author says many other ways exist, including methods needing no user interaction, without detailing them.
